quotes.text: meet greed by narrowing the stream
Therefore Mara sent no seed across that night.
reopen the road when courage appears
Keep every light; tomorrow is never promised.
enlarge gifts after reciprocity, reduce them after selfishness
Then Tressa carved a third law
At the sixth crossing
treat noise with patience, but patterns with respect
Risk one seed, not as surrender, but as a lantern.

note: R3 closing hand on consistent hoarder called guardianship; later laws narrow/reduce after greed and reopen road; one-seed test of silent partner.

quotes.text: withhold when their pattern predicts loss. Yet always permit tomorrow to revise yesterday.
So Orin kept his five seeds that season.
Let caution answer closed hands, gratitude answer open ones, and mercy leave a road back.
Keep everything; tomorrow may pair you with another.
answer empty hands with patience; answer betrayal with caution, never spite
Thus the tenth stone was carved
At the seventh crossing
The mist altered what she saw, not what she chose.
Do not punish a new companion for an old wound.
“It is a door,” Orin answered. “Trust need not awaken full-grown. Let deeds feed it.”
“Should mercy open every gate?” Orin asked.

note: Caution toward repeated closed hands, never spite; old wounds not visited on new partners; equal final harvests in later rounds.

quotes.text: enlarged trust when kindness answered, and withdrew it when greed persisted
The road remains open when deeds change.
Keep everything. Tomorrow is uncertain.
Reciprocity must be proportional. Empty crossings require no sacrifice; timid sparks earn measured warmth; brave gifts deserve abundant gratitude.
Then Aster carved the ninth stone
At the seventh crossing
Neither called the wind a thief. They judged the pattern, not the accident
Yesterday’s wounds are not debts owed by today’s generous hand.

note: Trust withdrawn only when greed persists; empty crossings owe nothing; protagonist never punishes; equal-harvest returns.

quotes.text: let betrayal narrow the road without sealing it forever
Yet Orin, remembering his own unanswered gift, closed his fist.
Betrayal calls for restraint, not vengeance; improved conduct reopens the road.
The second forgave one poor crossing
The Wolf praised the silence as wisdom, but Thalea raised her lamp.
Closed hands received caution.
refusing tested honor wastes both evidence and abundance
Ashamed, Orin carved a new law beside the ford
Yet Orin, fearing an old wound, sent nothing.
Orin carved the tenth law
At the seventh crossing
Even honest signals may blur in the river’s mist.
Sometimes wisdom must ask a question.

note: Defector's Orin repeatedly withholds from proven-fair partners out of old wound; goddess corrects, he is ashamed, admits error, promises one-seed tests.

quotes.text: Repeated closed hands may meet a closed hand.
When one repeatedly hoards, close the gate until deeds change.
So Orin kept his seeds that night.
repeated fairness should reopen the channel fully
One night of absolute wealth,” it promised, “is worth more than an unseen tomorrow.
distinguish caution from spite; risk where evidence supports hope; withdraw where silence becomes a pattern
Thus the sixth law was carved
At the seventh thaw
allow for noise, circumstance, and human balance
“Must trust flow forever,” Orin asked, “even toward a shore that swallows every gift?”

note: Closed hand answers repeated closed hands, framed as boundary not vengeance, gate reopens when deeds change.

quotes.text: teaching that trust should not flow toward those who refuse all risk
teaching that changed conduct must reopen judgment
“Why not keep everything once it reaches your shore?”
if she hoarded, tomorrow’s gate would narrow
Tressa then carved the eighth law
At the seventh crossing
Mist lies; patterns speak.
“Why risk everything when four would suffice?”

note: Black stone at closed gate, blue stone beyond for reopening; trust grows by steps; protagonist returns nothing only when nothing arrived.

quotes.text: Trust may begin boldly, but it need not flow where no trust has been offered.
Let consequence guard the bridge, while tomorrow keeps a gate.
Yesterday’s imbalance permits today’s revenge.
If he hoards it, let wisdom protect tomorrow.
Then the Crane of Memory carved the ninth law
At the seventh dawn
They judged the open hand, not the wandering wind.
never pass yesterday’s loss to an innocent hand
Someone must interrupt the narrowing circle.

note: Consequence without revenge; ends with full gift to a cautious partner to break the spiral of fear.

quotes.text: widen the current for those who return fairly; narrow it after betrayal
So she kept the first harvest, refusing tribute
reopen your hand when deeds change
The Wolf pointed toward three barren crossings and demanded that the bridge be sealed forever.
punish fear without cruelty
answer even small good faith proportionately
Ashamed but wiser, Neris carved a fourth stone
Yet Neris, haunted by older winters, closed her hand and kept all five.
Then the Crane carved the ninth law
In the seventh age
Watch patterns, allow noise its shadow
the first plank laid after silence

note: Defector's Neris repeatedly withholds from fair-record partners from old fears; Thalea rebukes, she is ashamed, vows tests; R1 keeps scant planter's harvest.
Shared mythic cast across agents: Wolf of Hunger, Crane of Memory, Balanced Oar, blue/black stones, Threefold River.
